top_candidate_demo_scenarios.title: KG-RAG improves recall over standard RAG for Czech public-health analytical scope retrieval
top_candidate_demo_scenarios.short_description: A controlled comparison where standard RAG retrieves text/table chunks directly, while KG-RAG first expands user disease-group and category phrases through MKN-10-CZ and code-list relations before retrieval and scope construction.
top_candidate_demo_scenarios.dataset: infectious_diseases primary table with MKN-10-CZ and age-group code lists as semantic support
example_questions: For the user query “Compare intestinal infectious diseases in the Czech Republic”, which exact diagnosis codes must be retrieved before any answer is generated?
For “Compare intestinal infectious diseases across regions and age groups in recent years”, does the system recover the full typed scope needed for analysis?
Can the system explain which intestinal-infection codes are represented in the table, which relevant MKN code is absent, and which lexical match is outside the target group?
top_candidate_demo_scenarios.standard_rag_version: Embed and retrieve table-value chunks, row-group summaries, and metadata snippets; infer selected codes and dimensions from top-k retrieved text.
top_candidate_demo_scenarios.kg_rag_version: Link the user phrase to typed MKN/code-list entities, expand through code-label-hierarchy relations, constrain retrieval to expanded codes/dimensions, and expose the selected analytical scope before summarization.
top_candidate_demo_scenarios.expected_benefit_to_test: KG-RAG should improve exact diagnosis-code recall, typed analytical-scope recall, and coverage/precision explanations over standard RAG on the three exact evaluation questions.
top_candidate_demo_scenarios.baseline_retrieval_risk: A lexical proxy for `střev` retrieves only 4 of 9 in-table A01-A09 gold codes, and includes B81 outside the A00-A09 range.
risks: Standard dense RAG may recover more than the lexical proxy; this must be measured, not assumed.
Manual query paraphrase sets are required for fair recall evaluation.
KG expansion must mark A00 as absent from the infectious table rather than hallucinating rows.
Counts are reported case counts and must not be framed as prevalence, incidence, treatment guidance, or causal evidence.

warnings: Final comparison remains a design/evaluation plan; no RAG, KG-RAG, KG, or SQL QA implementation has been built.
next_steps: Review official metadata/methodology before using epidemiological terminology.
Create typed value indexes and gold sets for recall evaluation.
Evaluate exact lexical/vector baselines before adding KG or semantic expansion.
Keep the first demo one-table-first unless supporting code-list coverage is clearly useful.
final_demo_direction: Compare standard RAG with KG-RAG for recall of typed analytical scope, using intestinal infectious diseases A00-A09 as the primary gold case.

mkn10_hierarchy_mapping_outputs.note: Diagnosis and chapter fields are from the ÚZIS open MKN-10-CZ CSV; block fields are derived because the open CSV has no explicit block columns.

final_research_questions.question: Does KG-RAG improve exact diagnosis-code recall over standard RAG for Czech disease-family queries whose table labels do not all share the user’s wording?
final_research_questions.why_important: This is the core scientific claim: KG hierarchy expansion should recover codes that pure retrieval may miss.

final_research_questions.question: Does KG-RAG improve typed analytical-scope construction for SQL/table answers involving informal Czech time, age, and region expressions?
final_research_questions.why_important: The demo will answer through SQL/rendered tables, so the system must recover the exact scope before aggregation.

final_research_questions.question: Can KG-RAG preserve or improve precision and provenance while increasing recall, especially for absent hierarchy members and lexical outsiders?
final_research_questions.why_important: A top demo paper needs to show KG expansion is controlled, inspectable, and not just broader retrieval.
